headline: Anthropic's debut couldn't hold the AI bid: a broad sell-off into the close, and gold sold with stocks

findings.headline: The morning AI rally reversed into one of the broadest down days of the year
findings.body: Anthropic opened at $111.50 against an $83 IPO price and faded to $97.17, and the AI names it had lifted (Nvidia, Micron, CoreWeave) flipped from early gains to losses. Only 37 S&P 500 stocks rose against 446 that fell, and it was a sixth straight loss that leaves the index 8.2% below last month's record. Analysts found no single catalyst; one plausible factor is that the record $81 billion offering made funds sell other holdings to make room for it.

findings.headline: AMD's China exposure is now in the spotlight, and the export-rule deadlines are dated
findings.body: AMD closed down 7.7% after Hunterbrook, which is short the stock, alleged that blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT kept getting newer AMD firmware. AMD says the claims misrepresent its practices, and the report itself does not show a violation. The part that matters beyond one stock is the rules: a new licence requirement for advanced chips shipped to Singapore and four other countries took effect today, and the suspension of the rule covering firms 50% owned by blacklisted entities runs out on 10 January 2027.

findings.headline: No haven bid: gold fell with stocks to its lowest since September 2025
findings.body: Gold usually catches a bid on a day like this, but it hit a 14-month low because futures fully price a December Fed hike after Wednesday's minutes showed almost all officials expect higher rates. A firm dollar and Treasury yields that barely fell confirm it: the market is selling risk because of tighter policy, not buying safety. Friday brings Fed Governor Waller at 14:25 and Cook at 18:15 Zurich, with final Michigan sentiment and inflation expectations at 16:00; Monday's flash PMIs are the next real test of the December hike pricing.

view: Our view: when gold, small caps and AI all fall together while bonds don't rally, the cause is tighter policy rather than fear, so it won't fix itself on a good headline. We would not buy the dip until the flash PMIs or Fed speakers soften the case for a December hike.
